title: Improved the event to mention the tool when a single tool use, or be a button that shows the list of used tools
summary: When an AI in a chat uses tools (like searching verses or going to a passage), the chat used to say only "Apologist used a tool" or "Apologist used 3 tools", without saying which ones. Now a single tool use names the tool (for example "Apologist used `goToReference`"), and a run of several tool uses becomes a button that opens a list of every tool name, in the order they were used. Chats with no tool uses should look exactly as before.

links.label: Issue 2047: AI chat: show which tools the AI used

setup.title: Open the preview build on a computer
setup.body: Use Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop. Open the **Open the preview build** link at the top of this page. It ends in `?autoinstall-ext_Apologist=true`, which installs the Apologist AI for you; if Seed Bible asks whether to install it, say yes. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload.

setup.title: Make sure you have the new version
setup.body: The app saves a copy of itself in your browser, so it can show an older version. Do a hard refresh once: **Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, or **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac.

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Sign in with your email. Seed Bible emails you a code, so use an address whose inbox you can check.

setup.title: Know how to start an AI chat
setup.body: Open **John 3**, click **John 3:16** so it's selected, then click **Ask AI** in the toolbar. If a menu of AIs opens, pick **Apologist**. If a **Before you chat with AI** box appears, tick its checkbox. You can clear the text Ask AI put in the message box and type your own message instead. To start a fresh chat later, use the **+** button in the chat panel.

setup.title: About the AI's answers
setup.body: The AI decides for itself which tools to use, so its exact tool names and counts can differ from the examples here. Tool names look like computer words, for example `goToReference`, `searchVerses` or `searchTranslations`. If a message doesn't get the AI to use the tools a test needs, start a new chat and try once more, rewording it a little. If it still doesn't, mark the test **Blocked** and paste what the chat showed in your notes.

sections.title: One tool use names the tool

tests.title: A single tool use shows the tool's name
tests.why: Issue 2047: "A single tool call shows the tool's name in the chat."
steps: Start an AI chat with Apologist (see setup).
Type `Please take me to Romans 8. Only use one tool.` and send it.
Wait for Apologist to answer, and look at the small grey line with Apologist's picture that appears between messages.
expected: The line reads **Apologist used** followed by the tool's name, for example **Apologist used `goToReference`**, not "Apologist used a tool".
The tool name is in a small box with a typewriter-style (code) font, sitting on the same line as the text.
The line is plain text: there's no arrow next to it and clicking it does nothing.
A time (like "now") still shows at the end of the line.

tests.title: The tool name is still there after a reload
tests.before: Use the chat from the previous test.
steps: Reload the page (**F5**, or **Cmd+R** on Mac).
Open the same chat again from the chat panel.
expected: The line still reads **Apologist used** with the same tool name in its code-style box.

sections.title: Several tool uses become a button with a list

tests.title: Several tool uses in a row show a count with an arrow, closed at first
tests.why: Issue 2047: "A group of tool calls shows '{Agent} used {N} tools'" and the list is "collapsed by default".
steps: Start a new AI chat with Apologist.
Type `Search for verses about hope, then search for verses about peace, then take me to the best verse you found. Don't write anything until you've done all three.` and send it.
Wait for Apologist to answer, and find the grey line that says how many tools it used.
expected: The line reads **Apologist used <number> tools**, for example **Apologist used 3 tools**, with a small down arrow after it.
No list of tool names shows yet.
Hovering over the text gives it a faint highlighted background, and the pointer becomes a hand.

tests.title: Clicking the line lists every tool in the order used
tests.why: Issue 2047: "expanding it lists every tool name in order."
tests.before: Use the chat from the previous test.
steps: Click **Apologist used <number> tools**.
Count the names in the list that opens.
expected: A row of tool names appears just under the line, each in its own small code-style box, centered under the line.
The number of names matches the number in the line (for example 3 names for "used 3 tools").
The names are in the order the AI used them. For the message above, that's normally the search tool first and the go-to tool last, for example `searchVerses`, `searchVerses`, `goToReference`.
The arrow now points up, and the line keeps its highlighted background while the list is open.

tests.title: Using the same tool twice lists it twice
tests.why: On the issue, the maintainer agreed that each use is listed, even repeats of the same tool, to show exactly what the AI did.
tests.before: Use the open list from the previous test.
steps: Look for a tool name that appears more than once in the list (with the message above, the search tool usually does).
expected: A tool used twice appears twice in the list, and both count toward the number in the line. Names are not merged into one.
If the AI happened to use each tool only once, write that in your notes and mark this test **Skip**.

tests.title: Clicking again hides the list
tests.before: Use the open list from the previous test.
steps: Click **Apologist used <number> tools** again.
expected: The list of names disappears and the arrow points down again.
Nothing else in the chat moves around or changes.

tests.title: The list opens and closes with the keyboard
tests.why: Issue 2047: "The expand control works with the keyboard."
tests.before: Use the chat from the previous tests, with the list closed.
steps: Click once in an empty part of the chat messages, away from any button.
Press **Tab** (and **Shift+Tab** to go back) until the **Apologist used <number> tools** line is highlighted.
Press **Enter**.
Press **Space**.
expected: When the line is reached with **Tab**, a clear outline shows around it.
**Enter** opens the list of tool names.
**Space** closes it again (and doesn't scroll the page).

tests.title: A screen reader says whether the list is open
tests.why: Issue 2047: the control "announces whether it's expanded or collapsed."
tests.before: Only if you use a screen reader (VoiceOver on Mac: **Cmd+F5**; NVDA or Narrator on Windows). Otherwise mark this test **Skip**.
steps: Move the screen reader onto the **Apologist used <number> tools** line.
Activate it, then listen again.
Move into the list of names.
expected: The screen reader reads it as a button, for example "Apologist used 3 tools, button, collapsed".
After activating, it says "expanded" (or similar).
It doesn't read out a word like "keyboard arrow down" for the arrow.
It reads the tool names in the list, one after another.

tests.title: The line and list are easy to read in dark mode
steps: Switch Seed Bible to dark mode in its settings.
Open the chat that has **Apologist used <number> tools** and open the list.
Also look at the chat with the single tool name.
expected: The text, the arrow, and the tool-name boxes are all clearly readable on the dark background. Nothing is black-on-dark or invisible.
The highlighted background behind the open button is visible but subtle.

tests.title: Tool names fit on a phone-width screen
steps: Make your browser window narrow, about the width of a phone, and reload (or open the preview link on a phone and sign in with the same account).
Open the chat that has **Apologist used <number> tools** and open the list.
expected: The names wrap onto more lines if needed, and stay inside the chat panel: nothing runs off the right edge and you don't need to scroll sideways.
The button and its arrow are easy to tap.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: A chat where the AI uses no tools looks the same as before
tests.why: Issue 2047: "Chats with no tool calls look the same as today."
steps: Start a new AI chat with Apologist.
Type `In one sentence, what is grace? Don't use any tools.` and send it.
expected: Your message and Apologist's reply show as usual.
No "used" line, button or list of names appears anywhere in the chat.

tests.title: Join messages in a shared chat still show
steps: Use a second browser (or a private/incognito window) signed in with a different email address.
In the first browser, start a shared session and invite the second browser into it.
Join from the second browser, then look at the session's chat in the first browser.
expected: The chat shows a grey line like **<name> joined**, as before, with no arrow or button.
If you can't set up a shared session, mark this test **Blocked** and say why in your notes.

notCovered: What each tool was given or sent back. Issue 2047 leaves this out on purpose; only tool names are shown.

The extension screens that say where an extension came from ("From <site>" or "Version … · from <site>" on an extension added from a link). This PR moved the code that builds that text into a shared file without changing what it shows, and it's only visible for extensions added from a third-party link, which testers usually don't have.
Other languages: the new "<name> used <tool>" wording is only in English so far; other languages show English for it until translators add it.
